- **`iss` (Issuer)**: Identifies the principal that issued the JWT.
- **`sub` (Subject)**: Identifies the principal that is the subject of the JWT.
- **`aud` (Audience)**: Identifies the recipients for whom the JWT is intended.
- **`exp` (Expiration Time)**: Identifies the expiration time on or after which the JWT must not be accepted for processing.
- **`nbf` (Not Before)**: Identifies the time before which the JWT must not be accepted for processing.
- **`iat` (Issued At)**: Identifies the time at which the JWT was issued.
- **`jti` (JWT ID)**: Provides a unique identifier for the JWT.

---

### Are Any Claims Mandatory?

No. None of the registered claims are mandatory to use under RFC 7519. Every registered claim is optional, leaving requirement rules to specific application contexts.

### Supporting Quote

Section 4.1 states:

> "None of the claims defined below are intended to be mandatory to use or implement in all cases, but rather they provide a starting point for a set of useful, interoperable claims."

(Sections 4.1.1 through 4.1.7 further confirm this individually, each concluding: *"Use of this claim is OPTIONAL."*)
